lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The résumé includes personal details that are conventionally left off.
items.because: Date of birth and nationality take space and draw attention away from professional evidence.

items.says: Education appears before the recent engineering experience.
items.because: Leading with education delays the strongest evidence for the candidate’s current direction.

items.says: The dates show a 10-month period with no study or work listed.
The 35% accuracy gain lacks a baseline and evaluation context.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it is a relative increase or percentage points, or verify the gain.

items.says: The disagreement reduction is buried after the routing-layer description.
The tool-call and latency reductions are buried after a long method description.
The release-safety result is buried after the evaluation scope.
Assistant-only loss masking does not train the model to reproduce tool-output tokens.
items.because: It excludes tool-output tokens from the training loss.

items.says: This bullet repeats the assistant-only loss-masking work in the first bullet.
items.because: The repetition uses space that could distinguish separate contributions.

items.says: The purpose clause describes an intended result, not a measured improvement.
items.because: Without a comparison point and evaluation context, the line does not establish improved tool-output fidelity.

items.says: The 68% backlog reduction comes after the system description instead of leading with the result.
“ML-extracted features” does not identify the feature-extraction approach.
Switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision alone does not support a fourfold reduction in total GPU memory.
items.because: Fine-tuning memory includes components such as optimizer states, so mixed precision does not guarantee that reduction.

items.says: The two nearby uses of “by” make the sentence awkward.
The release-cycle claim gives the endpoint but no starting point.
items.because: Without a before-and-after comparison, a reader cannot tell how much faster cycles became.

items.says: The sentence shifts from past tense to present tense.
The dispatch improvement has no measure of the backlog or delay change.
items.because: The 30-service count shows scope, not how much morning dispatch improved.

items.says: The migration result is not the opening focus of the bullet.
The claimed downstream benefits do not say what changed or how it was measured.
items.because: A reader cannot judge what downstream teams gained.

items.says: “AI-first engineering practices” does not identify a practice used to drive adoption.
The context limit is not connected to an outcome it enabled.
“The raw conversation grew 100x” does not make clear what grew by 100 times.
The line gives the concurrency condition but not how much the fix reduced failures.
items.because: The 50-way condition shows test scale, not how frequently failures occurred or how much they fell.

items.says: The concurrency fix and its result do not lead the bullet.
“50-way fan-out” is specialized jargon that may obscure the test scale.
The integration’s outcome is missing.
items.because: The metric count shows scope, but not why the contribution mattered to the framework or its users.

items.says: The metric categories do not show what the metrics measure.
items.because: Without an example, a reader cannot tell what evaluation capability they provide.

items.says: The correlation is not defined clearly enough to interpret the validation result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which quantities produced it, how it relates to the trials, or exactly what was removed.

items.says: The strongest evaluation result is not the opening focus of the bullet.
The validation result does not say what the evaluator’s ability enabled.
This bullet repeats the industrial-inspection triage result under the research-agent project and gives a slightly different reduction figure.
items.because: The matching signal count and backlog outcome identify the same achievement, while the different figure leaves readers unsure which is correct.

items.says: The backlog reduction has no time period or comparison point.
items.because: A reader cannot tell over what period it occurred or what it was measured against.

items.says: The line does not say what the triage branch screens the signals for.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what condition or issue it identifies.

items.says: The bullet uses present tense for a project dated Feb–Jul 2025.
items.because: “Screens” reads as ongoing work although the project dates indicate it has ended.
